title: AI Customer Communication and Service Quality

questions.question: What is the main risk of AI-assisted service replies?
options: They always include too much empathy, which makes replies feel insincere to customers
They can sound professional while source confidence, empathy, or escalation is weak
They automatically remove every SLA commitment from the customer's original ticket
They cannot summarize a support ticket without a human rewriting it first
questions.explanation: The risk is a reply that sounds professional while source confidence, empathy, or escalation is actually weak — not excess empathy, removed SLA commitments, or an inability to summarize.

questions.question: A customer has already contacted support three times about the same billing error, and their fourth message uses noticeably sharper language than the earlier ones. Which of the lesson's four signals does this match most directly?
options: Customer frustration — repeated contact and escalating tone signal the customer is losing patience
Response uncertainty — the AI-drafted reply is not confident the proposed fix is correct
SLA risk — the response is at risk of missing a committed service-level deadline
Escalation need — the issue requires a human specialist the AI cannot substitute for
questions.explanation: Repeated contact with escalating tone is the lesson's customer-frustration signal — distinct from response uncertainty (an unconfident draft), SLA risk (a deadline), or escalation need (needing a human specialist).

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A final, legally binding customer contract ready for signature
A complete support ticketing database that replaces the existing CRM
A ranked customer-response quality plan with controls for each scenario
An automatic refund issued directly to the customer without review
questions.explanation: The artifact ranks scenarios into a customer-response quality plan with controls — it doesn't generate a contract, replace the support database, or issue refunds automatically.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: Escalation path — a defined route to a human specialist when confidence is low
Hiding uncertainty from the customer so the reply reads as fully confident
Skipping the empathy check because the reply is factually accurate anyway
Ignoring SLA risk since the reply already answers the customer's question
questions.explanation: The lesson's controls are response source, empathy check, confidence threshold, and escalation path — escalation path routes low-confidence cases to a human, unlike hiding uncertainty, skipping empathy, or ignoring SLA risk.

questions.question: When should AI-assisted customer communication receive stronger review?
options: Only when no customer is directly affected by the support interaction at all
Only when the AI-drafted answer is already fully certain and source-backed
Never — a warm, empathetic tone by itself is always a sufficient review
When customers are frustrated, confidence is low, SLA is at risk, or escalation is needed
questions.explanation: Customer frustration, low response confidence, SLA risk, or a clear escalation need are exactly the signals that call for stronger review — not the absence of an affected customer, full certainty, or tone alone.

questions.question: What should be checked before sending an AI-assisted service reply?
options: Only grammar and spelling, since tone and accuracy are handled elsewhere
Source evidence, an empathy check, a confidence threshold, and an escalation path
Only the word count of the reply, to keep responses short and consistent
No ticket context at all, since the AI reply is expected to stand on its own
questions.explanation: Before sending, the lesson checks source evidence, an empathy check, a confidence threshold, and an escalation path — not just grammar, word count, or a reply written without ticket context.
